subject: checks-and-balances
title: Three Branches, One Team
summary: Why the U.S. government is split into three parts that check each other.

cards.title: Rock, paper, scissors
cards.text: In rock, paper, scissors, nothing wins every time. The people who wrote the U.S. Constitution wanted government to work a bit like that. Why would they want no single part to always win?

cards.title: Three branches
cards.text: The Constitution splits the national government into three branches. Congress makes laws. The President leads the executive branch and makes sure laws are carried out. The courts decide what laws mean and whether they follow the Constitution.

cards.title: Checks: the veto
cards.text: Congress can pass a bill, but the President can veto it, which means saying no. Then Congress can still make it a law if two thirds of both the House and the Senate vote yes.
cards.example: Two thirds is a lot. It is like needing 20 out of 30 kids in your class to agree.

cards.title: Checks: judges
cards.text: The President picks Supreme Court justices, but the Senate has to approve them. And the Supreme Court can strike down a law that breaks the Constitution.

cards.title: Why do this?
cards.text: The goal is that no one person or group gets too much power. Each branch can push back on the others. That is called checks and balances.

cards.question: Checks and balances can make it slow and hard to pass laws. When is that a good thing? When might it be frustrating?
nudges: Think about a rule you would want to be very sure about.
Think about a problem that needs a fast fix.

options.why: Yes! Congress is the House and the Senate.
Courts decide what laws mean. Congress makes them.
The President can sign or veto bills, but Congress writes and passes them.

options.text: When the President says no to a bill
options.why: Right. But Congress can still override it with two thirds of each house.
A veto is the President rejecting a bill.
A veto stops a bill. It is not a law.

questions.q: Why did the Constitution set up checks and balances?

options.text: So no one person or group gets too much power
options.why: Exactly. Each branch can push back on the others.

options.text: So laws can be passed very fast
options.why: Checks often slow things down. The goal is balance of power.

options.text: So the President can do anything
options.why: The opposite. Checks limit every branch.

sources.title: Branches of the U.S. government
sources.supports: The three branches and their roles; checks and balances: the veto, Senate confirmation of nominees, removal of a president in exceptional cases, and the Court overturning unconstitutional laws.

sources.title: The Constitution of the United States: A Transcription
sources.supports: Veto override by two thirds of each House; the President shall "take Care that the Laws be faithfully executed"; Senate advice and consent for judges; House impeaches, Senate tries, two-thirds to convict, judgment limited to removal and disqualification.
